name: Pyrimidine synthesis
summary: Cytosol (one mitochondrial step). Unlike purines, the ring (orotate) is built first and then attached to PRPP. Carbamoyl phosphate synthetase II (rate-limiting, glutamine as N donor — vs CPS I in the urea cycle, which uses NH₃ and is mitochondrial) → carbamoyl aspartate → dihydroorotate → orotate (DHODH, leflunomide) → OMP → UMP (UMP synthase; deficiency = orotic aciduria). UMP → UDP → UTP → CTP; dTMP comes from dUMP via thymidylate synthase (5-FU) using methylene-THF, regenerated by DHFR (methotrexate, trimethoprim, pyrimethamine). Ribonucleotide reductase (hydroxyurea) makes the deoxy forms.

glutamine.name: Glutamine
glutamine.notes: Donates the nitrogen for carbamoyl phosphate (CPS II), unlike CPS I which uses free NH₃.

carbp.name: Carbamoyl phosphate
carbp.notes: Also made by CPS I for the urea cycle. In OTC deficiency, mitochondrial carbamoyl phosphate spills into this pathway → orotic aciduria with hyperammonemia.

orotate.name: Orotate
orotate.notes: Excreted in urine in orotic aciduria and in OTC deficiency.

dutp.name: Deoxyuridine triphosphate
dutp.notes: Kept low by dUTPase so uracil isn't built into DNA.

dump.name: Deoxyuridine monophosphate
dump.notes: Also made from dCMP by deamination.

dtmp.name: Deoxythymidine monophosphate
dtmp.notes: The only nucleotide made solely for DNA. Folate or B12 deficiency starves this step → megaloblastic anemia.

cps2.name: Carbamoyl phosphate synthetase II
cps2.notes: Rate-limiting; cytosolic; uses glutamine and 2 ATP. Activated by PRPP and ATP; inhibited by UTP. First domain of the trifunctional CAD protein.

atcase.name: Aspartate transcarbamoylase
atcase.notes: Second domain of CAD. (The rate-limiting step in bacteria, not humans.)

dhoase.name: Dihydroorotase
dhoase.notes: Third domain of CAD; closes the ring.

dhodh.name: Dihydroorotate dehydrogenase
dhodh.notes: The only mitochondrial step: inner membrane, passes electrons to CoQ. Inhibited by leflunomide/teriflunomide (RA, MS) — they block T-cell proliferation.

oprt.name: Orotate phosphoribosyltransferase
oprt.notes: First activity of the bifunctional UMP synthase; attaches the ring to PRPP. UMP synthase deficiency = hereditary orotic aciduria (autosomal recessive): orotic acid in urine, megaloblastic anemia that doesn't respond to B12 or folate, failure to thrive, no hyperammonemia. Treat with uridine.

odc.name: OMP decarboxylase
odc.notes: Second activity of UMP synthase (see orotate phosphoribosyltransferase).

ndk.name: Nucleoside diphosphate kinase
ndk.notes: Swaps a phosphate from ATP onto any NDP or dNDP.

ctps.name: CTP synthetase
ctps.notes: Aminates UTP using glutamine and ATP. Inhibited by CTP.

rnr.name: Ribonucleotide reductase
rnr.notes: Makes all deoxyribonucleotides from NDPs, using thioredoxin (NADPH). Inhibited by hydroxyurea (sickle cell, myeloproliferative disorders); gemcitabine also inhibits it. dATP is the master inhibitor (why ADA deficiency kills lymphocytes).

ts.name: Thymidylate synthase
ts.notes: Methylates dUMP with N⁵,N¹⁰-methylene-THF, which becomes DHF. Inhibited by 5-fluorouracil (as 5-FdUMP, a suicide inhibitor; capecitabine is its prodrug; leucovorin enhances it) and pemetrexed. DHF is recycled to THF by dihydrofolate reductase — inhibited by methotrexate (human), trimethoprim (bacterial) and pyrimethamine (protozoal); leucovorin (folinic acid) rescues methotrexate toxicity.
